title: Build immutable strategy market context and reference symbol binder
description:
Implement immutable MarketContext snapshots and a reference-symbol binder in mike_trade/market_data/context.py, with unit tests in tests/unit/test_market_context.py.

Required behavior:
- MarketContext is a frozen value object keyed by (symbol, as_of UTC, version). Version increases monotonically per symbol. A context carries:
  - latest quote and latest trade, with provider and receive timestamps
  - completed candles per timeframe as tuples of h.1 Candle objects
  - indicator values from h.2 calculators
  - feed identity (feed_id, a consolidated flag that is False for IEX)
  - freshness (data age relative to as_of, plus a stale flag and reason)
  - session status and session_id from the h.3 calendar
  - price_basis
  - an optional, non-required research context
  Collections are exposed read-only (tuples or MappingProxyType). Mutation attempts raise.
- A ContextBuilder assembles a snapshot from injected sources: candle builder state, indicator calculators, calendar, quote/trade cache, and clock. It performs no network or broker I/O and never fetches data on demand.
- Completed-bars rule: if a strategy declares completed bars only, the context it receives contains only CLOSED candles. A developing candle is included only when explicitly declared, and only in a separately named field.
- Feed and basis integrity: building a context from candles or quotes with mixed feed_ids, or with SPLIT_ADJUSTED history together with RAW prices intended for stop calculation, fails closed. It raises a typed error or yields a context marked invalid with a reason code. Stop-relevant prices are always exposed on the RAW basis.
- Selection: select_context(history, evaluation_time, max_age) returns the newest context with as_of <= evaluation_time that is fresh within max_age. Otherwise it returns an explicit STALE/MISSING result, never an older stale snapshot presented as fresh.
- Reference symbol binder: takes a strategy's declared inputs (primary symbol, optional declared reference symbols, timeframes, indicators, completed_bars_only) and returns a bound view of the declared symbols' contexts only. Accessing an undeclared symbol raises a typed error. Do not build any separate market-alert subsystem.
- Do not compute BUY or SELL decisions here.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/market_data/candles.py (h.1), mike_trade/strategies/indicators/core.py (h.2), and mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py (h.3)
- mike_trade/strategies/base.py and mike_trade/domain/strategy_types.py (if present) for the strategy input-declaration type
- mike_trade/market_data/cache.py, mike_trade/market_data/quality.py, and mike_trade/research/ports.py (if present) for quote/trade cache, freshness, and optional research types
acceptance_criteria: A test confirms that MarketContext and its nested collections are immutable: assigning a field or mutating a candle or indicator mapping raises.
A test confirms that version increases monotonically per symbol across successive builds, and that equal inputs at the same as_of produce equal contexts.
A test confirms that a strategy declaring completed_bars_only receives no DEVELOPING candle, even while one exists in the builder.
A negative test confirms that mixing an IEX series with a different feed_id is rejected or marked invalid with a reason code.
A negative test confirms that SPLIT_ADJUSTED history combined with RAW stop-reference prices is rejected or marked invalid, and that stop-relevant prices are exposed on the RAW basis.

Tests confirm that select_context returns the newest fresh snapshot at or before evaluation_time, ignores snapshots with as_of after evaluation_time, and returns an explicit STALE/MISSING result when no snapshot is within max_age.
A test confirms that the binder exposes declared reference symbols and raises a typed error on access to an undeclared symbol.
A test confirms that context carries feed_id with consolidated=False for IEX, plus session status and session_id from the calendar for a half-day session.
The module performs no network or broker I/O. Tests run with only injected fakes.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
modify candles.py, indicators/core.py, or calendar.py; adapt via their public APIs only
perform network, provider, or broker I/O or on-demand data fetching
add a separate market-alert subsystem for reference symbols
make BUY/SELL decisions in the context layer
run broad test suites or backtests
